notes.environment: Every ANTHROPIC_* variable of the environment is removed before a case runs: the anthropic SDK reads a base URL, default headers and more from them when a client is given none. No case is captured with one set.
notes.versions: The versions the fixture was written from. A message in Python's own words, which no replay compares, may name one: pydantic's names its version in a link.
notes.provenance: roomkit_commit is the commit roomkit was imported at, and roomkit_dirty whether the package's files had changes not committed then. Both are null unless the package's own files are tracked by the repository that holds them: a package installed inside some checkout is not that checkout's. catalogue holds what the provider read of its model's catalogue entry, which it reads whatever the endpoint: whether the catalogue knows the model, the tags among those the provider reads, and the least reasoning effort the entry declares. A case that changes because the catalogue changed shows it there.
notes.config: The keyword arguments of AnthropicConfig. The key is a placeholder.
notes.supports: supports_vision and supports_deferred_tools are what the provider of the case answers: whether its model takes images, and whether it can hold a tool declared and unseen. supports_streaming, supports_structured_streaming, supports_response_schema and supports_response_schema_with_tools are true for every configuration.
notes.request: AIContext dumped with model_dump(mode='json'), its ten request fields. A key the request carries is written masked there, and plain under request_api_key.
notes.before: The calls made on the provider of the case before the case's own, in order, each with its request, its request_api_key, its exchanges and what it gave. The case's own request, exchanges and expected are those of its last call, and stand alone: a replay that makes the last call only reads the same.
notes.exchanges.request: What Python sent: the method, the whole URL (scheme, host, a port that is written, path and query), the body as JSON with its members in the order sent, and five headers with each configured extra header: x-api-key and authorization, with a key replaced by which key it was (<config key> or <request key>), anthropic-version, content-type and accept. A header that was not sent is null. RoomKit decides the key and the extra headers; the anthropic SDK decides the three others, which the endpoint reads. The other headers of the SDK and of the platform are left out. timeouts holds, in seconds, how long the request may wait to connect, for a read, for a write and for a connection of the pool. Every generation is asked as a stream: generate and generate_stream read the same stream generate_structured_stream gives.
notes.exchanges.response: What the fake answered: status and headers with a body under json, under text for a body that is no JSON, or under chunks for a body read in several reads. Each chunk is the bytes of one read, in order: a text where the bytes are UTF-8, written as that text, else an object whose hex member holds the bytes in hexadecimal, as a read that ends inside a character is. then says how the reads end after them: the stream ends, the connection is lost, or the read times out. A failure in place of a response is under failure: no answer came.
notes.exchanges.wait: The wait the anthropic SDK took before its next try, in seconds, and where it came from: the answer's headers, or the SDK's backoff, which is up to a quarter less than what is written. An HTTP date is read against clock.
notes.expected: What Python returned: response for generate (AIResponse without tasks and observations), text for generate_stream (the deltas), events for generate_structured_stream (each event dumped), models for list_models (each ModelInfo dumped). A failure is under error, after whatever a stream gave first: its class, its message (the first argument), its text (str), the attributes of a ProviderError, and raised_from, the class of the SDK or transport error it was raised from, if any.
notes.compare: On a call that fails, how a replay compares the failure. exactly lists what it reproduces as written: attributes of the error, reason among them where the error is a response schema's, and events or text, what the stream gave before it failed. An empty list is a failure no provider reproduces: the SDK's own, or a raw Python exception. message says whose words the message holds, and so whether it is compared: roomkit (RoomKit's own words: compared), server (the text the server sent, handed on as it came: compared), sdk (the anthropic SDK's words: not compared), python_json (what Python's JSON reader says of a text: not compared), python_repr (Python's repr of the JSON the server sent, of an error body after 'Error code: <status> - ' and of a stream's error event alone: not compared), transport (the HTTP client's words for a body it could not read to its end: not compared), python (the words of a Python exception raised while the answer was read: not compared). A python_json message leaves RoomKit's own words before it uncompared too ('the answer is not a JSON document (...)'). A compared roomkit message may hold Python's repr of a name or of a list (tool 'orders.lookup', missing ['city']), which a replay writes the same way.
notes.minted_call_ids: The ids in expected that Python minted for a call its server gave no id of its own: call_<name>_<12 hexadecimal digits>, random. A replay compares their shape, and that the events of one call share one id, not their value.
notes.sdk: Where a case says sdk, the anthropic SDK decided the behaviour, not RoomKit: its retries (which answers, how many times, after what wait), how it joins a URL, merges a body or follows a redirect, how it reads a stream's events, and the words of a failure that has no answer. A provider without that SDK decides these itself.
notes.questioned: Where a case says questioned, it pins a behaviour of Python that is not settled, in the sentence given, which starts with its kind. 'A possible defect': what looks like a defect of Python, to report upstream. 'A difference to decide': a point where the Rust provider is planned otherwise, which the maintainer decides; no defect is claimed. A replay may set the case aside, or expect otherwise once it is settled. The fixture lists their names under questioned.
